sections.title: The letter pé
paragraphs: The name of this letter sounds like (pé) /pe/. It usually makes the sound /p/, as in the word (porte) /pɔʁt/, which means door. This letter has one spoken sound, but it can also stay completely silent.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Close both lips firmly together to stop the air. Then open your lips quickly to let the air pop out. Keep your vocal cords still so they do not buzz. Hold your hand before your mouth. You should feel only a very gentle breath.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: This letter makes the sound /p/ at the beginning or inside a word, as in (pomme) /pɔm/. It is usually silent at the very end of a word, as in (drap) /dʁa/ and (trop) /tʁo/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: In English words like pat, a strong puff of air escapes. In French, you must release your lips with very little air. Hold a light paper strip before your face. The paper must hardly move when you speak.
